checks_performed.check: Lock hold time introduced by list_dicts
checks_performed.method: /mnt/session/outputs/probes/lock_hold.py (in-process, head storage).
checks_performed.result: GET /todos now holds the store lock while building every dict: about 5 ms at 1k todos, 31 ms at 10k, 244 ms at 50k, against the base pattern's 0.1/0.8/5.4 ms (sort only). Not raised: the lock is what keeps done and overdue consistent within an element under concurrent complete() (asdict and is_overdue read `done` separately), and an in-memory sample service does not hold 10k+ todos. Related, also not raised: POST /todos calls to_dict() outside the lock as the spec prescribes, so a complete() on the just-created id between asdict and is_overdue could in principle yield done:false/overdue:false for a past-due todo in that one POST response. The window needs the client to guess the id before the create returns.

findings.claim: No test in the test plan pins the UTC half of the overdue rule. If app.storage.today_utc is changed to return the host-local date (`date.today()`), all 37 pytest tests, `local-all` and `rollover-local` still pass. Every pytest clock test monkeypatches today_utc away, and local-all starts the server with the caller's environment, which is UTC on the orchestrator and in this sandbox. A regression to local time would therefore merge green, even though the goal defines overdue as 'strictly before the current UTC calendar date'.

evidence.reproduction: bash /mnt/session/outputs/probes/f1_local_clock_mutant.sh   (clones head to /tmp/f1, applies `return date.today()` in app/storage.py:11, runs the plan's pytest / local-all / rollover-local, then the same live checks against a server started with a TZ whose date differs from UTC; full output in /mnt/session/outputs/probes/f1_local_clock_mutant.out)
evidence.observed: UTC now 2026-10-10T12:23:27, Pacific/Kiritimati date 2026-10-11. Mutant: `python -m pytest -q` -> 37 passed; with TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati -> 37 passed; `python tests/e2e_overdue.py local-all` -> 10 passed, 0 failed; rollover-local -> 1 passed. The same checks against the mutant started with TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati: FAIL boundary ('due 2026-10-10 with UTC today 2026-10-10: POST overdue True, want False'), FAIL listing, FAIL overdue-list (e2e-overdue-e, due today, is listed as overdue).
evidence.expected: At least one test_plan command fails when today_utc stops returning the UTC calendar date, as the plan already does for the other halves of the rule (`<=` instead of `<`, ignoring done, an unsorted list).

violates: spec.goal: 'overdue iff open and due_date strictly before the current UTC calendar date'
findings.refutation_condition: Withdrawn if the implementer shows a test_plan command (pytest or the local e2e entries, run in an environment whose TZ is UTC, like the orchestrator's) that fails on head with app/storage.py:11 replaced by `return date.today()` (and by `return datetime.now().date()`), or shows that the orchestrator's local or preview runs always use a host time zone whose calendar date differs from UTC.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) in tests/test_overdue.py, monkeypatch `app.storage.datetime` with a datetime subclass whose `now(tz=None)` returns a fixed instant such as 2026-11-30T23:30:00Z converted to `tz` (or to a +10:00 local wall time when tz is None), and assert `app.storage.today_utc() == date(2026, 11, 30)` (this avoids the grep-forbidden strings); or (b) in tests/e2e_overdue.py local_all, start uvicorn with `env={**os.environ, 'TZ': zone}`, choosing 'Etc/GMT-14' or 'Etc/GMT+12' so the server's local date differs from the UTC date at run time. The existing boundary/listing/overdue-list checks then catch it, as the reproduction shows.
